name: Memory-Insensitive Rendering
definition: A completely disk-based rendering technique for large unstructured volumetric grids that requires only a small, constant amount of main memory. It solves the problem of rendering arbitrarily large datasets on machines with limited memory by avoiding random access to the dataset.
summary: Memory-Insensitive Rendering is an out-of-core technique that renders large volumetric grids using constant main memory by avoiding random access through sequential disk scans and external sorting.
